speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; please describe the onset of these symptoms and whether the pain is localized to one wrist or both. Also, have you noticed any redness, swelling, or warmth in the affected area?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Septic Arthritis of the Left Wrist (suspected disseminated gonococcal infection given the travel history, preceding knee pain, and triad of fever, migratory polyarthralgia, and tenosynovitis).

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP, Synovial Fluid Analysis (Left Wrist), and Gonorrhea/Chlamydia NAAT.
REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray Left Wrist and Left Knee.
